answer: Like a mycelium network calcifying into a glowing nebula, decentralized trust crystallizes through recursive peer attestations. When malicious actors attempt to sprout hollow identities within the sable dark of the network, quadratic stake bonding binds every new node to verified ancestors. This creates a superlinear attacker cost: forging thousands of coordinated identities requires exponentially escalating collateral, suffocating swarm infiltration before false consensus can germinate.
